clue.text: Artist returns to fabulous bird

indicators.note: returns tells us to read the run made by the next words from right to left

parts.note: the roc is the giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A painter goes back to depicting a legendary bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole run TO + ROC, giving COR + OT. Corot was the French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a nineteenth-century French landscape painter.

clue.text: Sweet girl?

explanation.surface: A sugary young lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a pudding of fruit baked in a bread or sponge case, and it is also a woman's given name.

clue.text: Earl of Huntingdon dressin for court?

explanation.walkthrough: Legend makes Robin Hood the Earl of Huntingdon. 'Dressin'' drops its final g, so robing (putting on robes, as a judge does for court) loses its g too.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood was given the title Earl of Huntingdon in later legend; a judge putting on robes before sitting in court is robing, said with a dropped g.

clue.text: Peg gives help in a row

definitions.text: Peg gives help in a row

parts.words: Peg gives help in a row
parts.note: a small peg on a boat's side that the oar pivots against, helping when one rows; 'row' looks like a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: A thole-pin is a peg set in the gunwale of a rowing boat to hold the oar in place as a fulcrum.

clue.text: Runner controlling heartbeat

explanation.surface: An athlete who keeps the heart ticking over.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who sets the speed for others in a race, and an electronic device implanted to regulate the heart's rhythm.

clue.text: Face familiar to Dickensians?

explanation.surface: A countenance well known to lovers of Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Phiz is old slang for the face (from physiognomy), and also the pen name of Hablot Browne, who illustrated Dickens's novels.

clue.text: Bloomers in 500 clues Alan composed

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Alan has written five hundred crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowering plants. D, CLUES and ALAN are rearranged together under 'composed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendulas, or pot marigolds, are garden plants grown for their flowers, so they are things that bloom.

clue.text: Comparatively silent actor?

explanation.surface: A performer who says even less than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as mum + -er, the word means more mum, i.e. quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum means silent, so a made-up comparative means quieter still; a mummer is a player in a traditional folk play, often performed in dumbshow.

clue.text: Bird interrupts cat-nap, so to speak?

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt as written

parts.note: to wake a kitty is to break into a cat's snooze

explanation.surface: A bird disturbs a cat's snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of northern seas.

clue.text: Miss Fleming's secret hoard

indicators.note: secret here means concealed, so the letters of the next word are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A woman named Fleming keeps a hidden stash.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhoda Fleming is the title heroine of a novel by George Meredith.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda Fleming is the heroine of George Meredith's 1865 novel of that name.

clue.text: Brother tucked into new salami! delicious!

indicators.note: tucked into means placed within, so one piece sits inside the other
new means freshly made, so the letters of salami are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A monk eats some fresh salami and finds it delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' reads like eating, but it is the container signal; the brother goes inside AMSIAL, made by 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, so ambrosial describes something divinely tasty.

clue.text: Tuberculin tested in cow product we hear, as a rule

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: the sound a cow produces is a moo
TT stands for tuberculin tested, a label once given to milk from TB-free herds

explanation.surface: Milk from tested cattle is the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: TT milk came from herds tested free of tuberculosis, a label well known in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short maxim adopted as a guiding principle of conduct.

clue.text: Bird helps to put ball in net

indicators.note: the letters are spread across the words, each contributing part of the run

explanation.surface: A bird assists in scoring a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sits in balL IN NET, each word helping to supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch known for its song.

clue.text: What spirit in a girl!

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly spirit

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a lively young woman's high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelina is a female given name.

clue.text: Johnson's friend who produced the poor, leg-break

indicators.note: break means smash into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's leg-break produced by a friend of Dr Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: James Oglethorpe, friend of Samuel Johnson, founded Georgia as a refuge for the poor and debtors; leg-break is a cricket delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: General James Oglethorpe, founder of the colony of Georgia, was a friend of Dr Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Go to bed with gout? Geting up's the answer

parts.note: to turn in is to retire for the night

explanation.surface: A gout sufferer wonders whether rising from bed will help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geting' is a misprint for 'getting'. TURN IN with GOUT attached gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to get out of bed in the morning.

clue.text: Dog that delights the shepherd?

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'red sky at night, shepherd's delight' makes a red setting sun the shepherd's joy.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter is the Irish setter gun dog, and a red sun going down is what the weather rhyme says pleases shepherds.

clue.text: Peel fruit, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the fruit is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: An instruction to peel some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to trim off the skin or outer layer.

clue.text: Alienates Tess badly about cooker

indicators.note: about means round, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
badly means poorly done, so the letters of Tess are disordered

parts.note: a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Tess's poor cooking puts people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooker' is the kitchen range, an everyday British word for a large stove; 'badly' makes ESTS and 'about' wraps it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make someone unfriendly or distant, so to alienate them.

clue.text: Book course director-about an hour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a tiller steers a boat's course
HR is the usual abbreviation for an hour

explanation.surface: A film director reads a novel for about an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' suggests film, but the course is a boat's, steered by the TILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a novel of suspense and excitement.

clue.text: Little boy finds revolver in river

explanation.surface: A small lad finds a gun in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a pet form of Edward, and an eddy is a whirling current of water, something that revolves in a river.

clue.text: Aloofness of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops keep their distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Detachment is emotional distance or indifference, and it is also a body of troops sent off on a separate task.

clue.text: Seen on stone in many an odd niche

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword way of saying many

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of niche are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A growth spotted on stone in many a strange alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichens are crusty growths of fungus and alga often found coating rocks and walls.

clue.text: What's the sense in, say. "" sea-power '?

annotationWithheld.clue: What's the sense in, say. "" sea-power '?

clue.text: Note birds under this part of the roof

parts.note: E is a musical note
Aves is the scientific name for the class of birds

explanation.surface: Birds nest under this projecting edge of a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaves are the overhanging lower edges of a roof.

clue.text: Mince pie offered by a place of entertainment

indicators.note: pie is a printers' word for jumbled type, so the letters of mince are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mince pie served at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like the pastry but is printers' slang for a jumble of type.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is a building where films are shown to the public.

clue.text: Goes out of play ?

parts.note: read as a stage direction: characters leave the stage during a drama

explanation.definitionFit: Exits are departures, and in a script the word marks actors leaving the stage.

clue.text: Girl the French notice

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Girl the French notice' (4) does not lead to the held answer XVIS; answer or clue is an OCR error with no scan to check.

clue.text: A number do engraving work in the plant

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
to etch is to engrave a design with acid

explanation.surface: Someone engraves a figure inside a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous climbing plant grown for fodder.

clue.text: Disgusting as some old peasants were

explanation.surface: Rebellious peasants of old were nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting means repulsive, and it also means rising in revolt, as in the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.

clue.text: Southern bookmakers' run. — ers

parts.note: printers make books, rather than taking bets

explanation.surface: Southern bookies' horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmakers' suggests betting, but printers literally make books.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinters are fast short-distance runners.

clue.text: Files in back of box about .Sunday opening

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
back of here means turned back, so the word for box is read backwards

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word Sunday

explanation.surface: Papers in the back of a box, opened on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' reverses SPAR to RAPS, which goes 'about' the S that 'opening' takes from Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps are coarse files used for shaping wood or metal.
